---
title: "Database Search"
---

All searches should use the group-approved FASTA database and documented software settings. Record database version, tool version, parameters, sample sheet, command, and output directory.

## Spectronaut

### Inputs

- Raw files
- Group-approved human FASTA plus `resources/fasta/Universal_Contaminants_381.fasta`, and, where applicable, a spectral library
- Sample metadata

### Checklist

1. Confirm raw-file names match the sample sheet.
2. Start from the validated group settings template.
3. Run a small representative subset first.
4. Review identification, quantification, and QC reports before full-scale analysis.

### Group-specific command

Add the approved Spectronaut module/container, script, FASTA path, and output convention here.

For the step-by-step library-free workflow, follow the [Spectronaut DirectDIA protocol](spectronaut-directdia.html).

## DIA-NN

### Hands-on Biowulf tutorial

Follow the group's **[How to Run DIA-NN on Biowulf](https://colossal-caper-1cd.notion.site/How-to-Run-DIANN-on-Biowolf-15fba19442768071ae0ff24d3a13e437)** guide for the detailed environment-specific workflow. Use it together with the group-approved FASTA, configuration, and storage paths.

### Library-free workflow

Use the documented human-plus-contaminants FASTA database and parameters appropriate for the instrument and digestion protocol. Review precursor and protein-level FDR settings before running.

```bash
diann --fasta <approved_database.fasta> \
  --f <raw_file_1> --f <raw_file_2> \
  --out <output_directory>/report.tsv \
  <lab-approved-parameters>
```

### Before accepting results

- Confirm the expected report and QC files were produced.
- Inspect identification numbers and retention-time behavior.
- Check that the sample names and output location are correct.
- Keep the exact command and log with the result files.
